This is a simple cover plate for a wall hole that provides a neat, orderly way to feed cables from your Home Theater system into the wall, or out of the wall at the TV Monitor location. It lets you buy one, long set of cables, rather than one set for inside the wall and two patch sets for home theater receiver to the wall, and wall to TV monitor. Things to know:
1. You will need TWO, if you are going to use a single set of cables!
2. You will need a old-work, low-power wall box for each one purchased. You can get these for $1-3 each (depending on style) at your local "Big-Box" hardware store. (Check both the electrical area and the home networking areas to find both styles.)
3. When planning your installation, recognize that the clump of wires coming out of the wall will not make many wives happy! Plan to have both boxes hidden by the TV or Home theater cabinet.
4. If moving connections horzintally from one wall location to another, you are likely to run into one or more studs. If you do not have experience with blind drilling large holes, you will be much happier

You write on them with a fine tip marker, fold one over the desired wire and stick the label to itself with the hook and loop fastener integrated on the back of the tag. It is stiff enough to resist folding or balling up, it can be removed and replaced numerous times to get a better fit or to move it to a better location on the wire.

The labels are only as clear as your handwriting - bad news in my case - but not a design flaw in the product. The labels, once written upon, are stuck with that label due to using a permanent marker. Keep the labels generic and perhaps this is not an issue.

These labels are easy to use, the positions can be adjusted on a wire as needed, and are strong enough to endure the stress of being pulled through other loops of wire when doing maintenance on your system.
